title: Topological Aspects of the $c=2$ Model in the Continuum and on the Lattice
authors: Yichul Choi, Nathan Seiberg, Sahand Seifnashri, Wucheng Zhang
abstract: We discuss the continuum two-dimensional conformal field theory, whose target space is a two-torus. In addition to its standard zero-form internal symmetries, the model also has a $-1$-form symmetry associated with its $θ$-parameter, which is also known as a background $B$-field. These symmetries combine into a higher group with anomalies. A spatially winding $B$-field generically breaks the spatial translation symmetry completely, and reduces the continuous target-space (internal) momentum symmetry to a (projectively realized) discrete subgroup. When $B$ varies linearly, a discrete translation subgroup survives, and it combines with the internal symmetry into a non-Abelian group, while the other translations survive as non-invertible symmetries. Even though the model lacks the standard spatial translation symmetry, the non-invertible translation symmetry explains why it is solvable via a Fourier decomposition. We then consider a lattice version of this system, using its modified Villain formulation. Surprisingly, all these subtleties in the symmetries of the continuum model exist on a finite lattice. Finally, we discuss various generalizations of this model, demonstrating that the phenomena we uncovered are more broadly valid.
summary: This work explores the topological symmetries of a $c=2$ CFT, examining how background fields modify its symmetry structure in the continuum limit. Crucially, the authors demonstrate that these complex symmetry behaviors, including the role of non-invertible symmetries, are faithfully reproduced when the model is discretized onto a finite lattice. This provides a powerful tool for studying topological order in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the topological aspects and symmetry structure of the $c=2$ conformal field theory (CFT) in both its continuum and lattice formulations.
main_result: It shows that the complex symmetry subtleties of the continuum model, including the role of background $B$-fields and non-invertible symmetries, are surprisingly preserved on a finite lattice using a modified Villain formulation.
method: The analysis combines continuum field theory techniques (using differential cohomology) with lattice regularization methods, specifically employing a modified Villain formulation for quantization.
model_or_system: The primary system is the $c=2$ CFT, modeled as a sigma model on a two-torus, characterized by compact scalar fields $\varphi_I$. The theory is analyzed under the influence of a background $B$-field, which can be spatially varying.
key_observables: Symmetry breaking patterns (e.g., reduction of continuous momentum symmetry to a discrete subgroup), non-Abelian symmetry groups, and the existence of non-invertible translation symmetries.
important_parameters: The background $B$-field, its winding number $K$, and the coupling constant $G$ (related to the sigma model metric).
main_assumptions: The continuum theory requires careful handling of correction terms during patch trivialization, and the solvability relies on the presence of non-invertible translation symmetries.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing the continuum theory (Section 2), specializing to the case of a linear $B$-field (Section 3), developing the Hamiltonian formulation (Section 4), detailing the lattice realization (Section 5), and concluding with a comparison of the continuum and lattice symmetries.
why_interesting: The deep connection between topological field theories, symmetry protection, and lattice regularization is highly relevant to understanding emergent symmetries in strongly correlated electron models, especially those involving gauge fields or topological order.
